paragraphs: Chapter 1041
Episode 249. The First Deployment of the Plutonian (8)
“Yes, Sister Goddess of Battle.”
Fzzzt-!

As soon as the order was given, the Battle Kings left afterimages as they flew in all directions. The first priests who discovered the Plutonian didn't even leave a piece of their white priestly robes behind, as they were instantly turned into ash by the blue lightning.
The place where the Plutonian arrived through the dimensional gate was the first temple of the Sun God Religion, located in a subspace.
In other words, it was essentially the headquarters of the Sun God Religion.

The Sun God Religion had to use ‘fragment’ to utilize Nirgand, and to procure these from the area of the Black Sea ruled by the five kings, the power of the largest temple was essential. The dimensional gate, which opened at the first place where the Sun God Religion encountered Nirgand, had never been closed.
That was why the Plutonian attacked the headquarters of the Sun God Religion in one fell swoop.
“Arghhh!”
“Cough…!”
The Battle Kings, who until moments ago had been laughing and joking as if they were bumbling brothers, showed no sign of mercy in their attacks.
Their attacks towards the nearby priests were merciless, filled with fierce intent to kill everything alive and breathing within the temple.
The annihilation of the Sun God Religion was not only a mission for Jin but also directly related to the honor of the Plutonian. After all, their former Battle God, Luke, was part of the group.
Every time the long swords of Baba and Baltiroc, and the great bow of Kaio flashed, parts of priests' bodies rolled on the ground.
Screams invited more thunderbolts, and those trying to flee couldn't take more than three steps.
Blood evaporates before hitting the ground due to the heat, and hastily drawn weapons and artifacts crumble like dry twigs.
Among the priests, there were quite a few noteworthy dead, but all were mere ants before the Plutonian.
Literally, a massacre.
Within ten seconds after the Plutonian passed through the dimensional gate, about a hundred priests lost their lives.

This was about 30% of the priests in the first temple. Since this was a temple where only the most faithful of the Sun God Religion could come, there weren't many priests residing there in the first place.
“Once a ruler of Lafrarosa, this temple is too pathetic to satisfy you, Luke. Hiding in subspace like a rat's nest… it's embarrassing.”
Thud, thud…!
Each step Vahn took spread cracks across the temple floor, sending vibrations throughout the building.
She was not in a hurry. From the moment she passed through the dimensional gate, she was confident that all the forces in this temple couldn't stop them.
It was subspace, after all. Escaping meant using another dimensional gate, which was impossible.
The entire temple was within Vahn's range. She already knew the number of people in the temple, their breathing, and even the flow of various energies, including Sun energy.
Thus, if any suspicious aura trying to open a dimensional gate was detected, she would simply bring down thunder on that spot.
Distant screams were heard. The cries of priests being annihilated by the scattered brothers who were searching and closing paths.
“Kelik! You and Tigrone block the west sector! I’ll go to the east gate…”
“We need support in the south!”
“Is the High Priest still not here…?”
The three Battle Kings were thoroughly trampling the priests flocking to their respective areas.

Occasionally, some outstanding priests managed to hold their own against the Battle Kings for a while. Those who did were legendary figures who had made their mark in the history of the martial world during their lifetimes.
Vahn entered the center of the temple and started walking down the long road stretching north. The priests called this road 'Holy Road,' and at the end stood the statue of the Sun God.
“Ah, no… the Holy Road… How dare you defile the sacred path to the Sun God, cough!”

A priest shouting like this met his death, suffocated by the lightning energy released by Vahn. The dazzling Holy Road, shining like daylight, was being eroded by the lightning energy. It was crumbling as if it were made of insignificant stones.
As it was a sacred path, many priests gathered to stop Vahn. These were the most faithful and brave priests.
Yet, even they couldn't rashly draw their weapons or scream.
Fear.
The first emotion the priests felt upon seeing Vahn was undoubtedly fear, as was always the case with the vast majority of her enemies.
After the fear passed, a strange desire to worship her surged up.
They were caught in an illusion. Could this person trampling on the Holy Road be the Sun God? Has He come to rebuke us?
"If not for that, how could they possess such power?" The priests were momentarily caught in such an illusion.
And before most of them could snap out of it, they met their death, suffocated by the lightning energy or burned, just like the priests who died earlier.
Black smoke was billowing from all around the temple. No one in the Sun God Religion could have anticipated that the first temple could be destroyed so futilely.
The buildings, which until moments ago shone beautifully in pure white, were nowhere to be found now, only ash and corpses filled the place.
The bright Holy Road now had only a few dozen steps left. No more screams were heard. Now, there were only five living priests in the temple.
One was Luke, and the other four were priests who didn't know how to fight. Luke was behind the closed doors of the sanctuary, and the priests were kneeling in front of the door, praying.
“Kinzelp will punish you.”
“The Lord will protect us. Our great Lord will save us…”

Vahn did not take the lives of the trembling, praying priests. They had information to be extracted. After all, this temple wasn't the only one. Vahn intended to extract information from them as soon as possible and destroy all the temples of the Sun God Religion, bringing about their ruin.
“Brother Kaio.”
Kaio, who had approached by her side, bowed to Vahn.
“Leave these priests alive. We will soon have a battle with the traitor, so take them and withdraw.”
“Yes.”
Kaio grabbed the priests and retreated to the back. Baba and Baltirock naturally followed Kaio.
Vahn had no intention of seeking her brothers' help when executing Luke. Not because they wouldn’t be of help, but because she wanted Luke to meet a more miserable end.

Vahn grabbed the firmly closed gates of the towering sanctuary that seemed to pierce the sky of subspace. She waved her hand lightly twice, as if brushing through bushes, and the giant iron doors were ripped apart and crashed to the ground.
Thud, thoom-!
The vast interior of the sanctuary was the only area not eroded by Vahn and the Battle Kings' lightning energy. Until now, Luke's energy had been blocking all the incoming lightning energy.
Vahn alternately looked at the back of Luke, who was kneeling and praying, and the giant statue in front of him.
Unlike the statue in the second temple, the statue in the first temple was an old-faced baby, and in its arms, the physical form of the Sun God shone faintly like a gold nugget.

“Luke, you have already experienced everything a living person could enjoy. Once, as the Battle God, you roamed the world at will, and everything bowed before you. What more did you want that you abandoned such glory?”
Eternal life, or meeting someone who had passed away.
There were only these two things that the Plutonian God in Luke's era could not achieve. Luke, however, gave an answer that Vahn never expected.
“More power.”
“…Power? That's unexpected. In your era, you were the absolute being with the greatest power.”
“No matter how much I conquered, the land was endless, the battles never ceased day or night, the endless struggle and victory. That is the right and destiny the Plutonian should rightfully have.”
Luke stood up.
Turning around, he had an expressionless face, but immense madness was writhing in his dry eyes.

“I chose to worship the Sun God to create such a world, Vahn. A world where we are not hindered by insignificant gods or special mortals, and one that remains unchanged even through the ages… A world where the true Plutonian exists.”
For a while, Vahn stared at Luke, speechless. The light from the body held by the statue was gathering towards Luke.
“In other words, you’re saying you fell for a cult, trying to forcibly create a world where only the Plutonian can eternally win and shine... Is that the right understanding?”
At those words, Luke shrugged his shoulders.
“Disappointing. I thought you, who ruled over more brothers and lands than I did and even dared to challenge the gods in your struggle, would understand me a bit.”
“I'm more disappointed, Luke. I wonder what face our ancestors who recognized such a scum as a God lived…”

“I have not forgotten our essence, and you have, Vahn. We are beings born to do anything for strength. You avoided destruction by seeking help from one of the hated gods, falling into the hands of a special mortal who is but a toy of that god, thereby diluting the blood of the Plutonian.”
The Sun God's ‘fragment’ was merging faster into Luke.
Unlike Nirgand, this power was not strengthening Luke. Luke was merely preparing to fight with the god he had chosen.

“In that sense, Vahn, you do not deserve to be called a God. Being a God is not just about being the strongest among us. It’s a title given to those who can lead us in the most characteristic way of us.”
After a moment of silence, Vahn shook her head.
“I've listened to your squeaking for too long. Come, it's time for your name to be recorded as the most shameful Plutonian in history.”
